label: thm:truncation-cost
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:truncation-cost}
Let $q=\mathcal{N}(0,C)$, $1\le K<d$ and $\eta>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] With $G_K:=\min\bigl\{1,\|(g_i)_{i>K}\|_2\bigr\}$, the ideal
truncated sampler satisfies
\[
 \tfrac1{100}\,G_K
 \;\le\;
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 \;\le\;
 \tfrac32\,G_K,
\]
and, with explicit constants,
$\mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta)\le\bigl(\frac18\sum_{i>K}x_i^2/(1+x_i)\bigr)^{1/2}$.
\item[(b)] For every probability law $p$ on $\mathbb{R}^K$, the truncated sampler
$\widetilde p^\eta$ of \eqref{eq:output-law} satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde p^\eta,q^\eta\bigr)
 \;\ge\;
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Cost of spectral truncation

label: thm:num-directions
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:num-directions}
Let $q=\mathcal{N}(0,C)$ with the exact power law \eqref{eq:powerlaw2}, and let
$\eta>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{Sufficiency.} For every $1\le K<d$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-tv}
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 \le\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{\eta^2\sqrt{8(2\beta-1)}}\,K^{-(2\beta-1)/2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the truncation error is at most $\varepsilon/2$ whenever
$K_\varepsilon(\eta)\le K<d$, where
\[
 K_\varepsilon(\eta)
 :=\biggl\lceil
 \Bigl(\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{\eta^2\,\varepsilon\sqrt{2(2\beta-1)}}\Bigr)^{2/(2\beta-1)}
 \biggr\rceil.
\]
\item[(b)] \emph{Necessity.} Let $\varepsilon<1/200$ and $2K\le d$. If some
truncated sampler that retains $K$ directions satisfies
$\mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p^\eta,q^\eta)\le\varepsilon$, then
\[
 K\ge k_\eta
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 K\ge\Bigl(\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2^{\beta}\cdot200\,\eta^2\,\varepsilon}\Bigr)^{2/(2\beta-1)}.
\]
\item[(c)] \emph{Where to cut.} If $k_\eta\le K$ and $2K\le d$, then the
first discarded direction has $x_{K+1}<1$, and
\begin{align*}
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 &\ge\tfrac1{100}\min\bigl\{1,\ 2^{-\beta-1}x_{K+1}\sqrt K\bigr\},\\
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 &\le\tfrac32\min\bigl\{1,\ c_\beta\,x_{K+1}\sqrt K\bigr\},
\end{align*}
with $c_\beta:=\sqrt{(2\beta+1)/(2\beta-1)}$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Number of retained directions

label: cor:noise-floor
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:noise-floor}
Under the exact power law, let $K=k_\eta\ge1$ and $2k_\eta\le d$. Every
truncated sampler that retains exactly the directions with variance at least
$\eta^2$ satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde p^\eta,q^\eta\bigr)
 \;\ge\;
 \frac1{100}\min\bigl\{1,\ 2^{-\beta-1}\sqrt{k_\eta}\bigr\},
\]
which is at least $1/100$ once $k_\eta\ge4^{\beta+1}$, however accurate the
sampler is in the retained directions.

label: ass:lipschitz
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:lipschitz}
For every $t\in[0,T]$, the law $q_{K,t}$ has a $C^2$ density whose score
$\nabla\log q_{K,t}$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and the tail and regularity conditions
of Appendix~\ref{app:general-rates} hold.
head: environment
name: Score regularity

label: ass:score_error
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:score_error}
The score estimates used by the sampler satisfy
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N
 \mathbb{E}_{U\sim q_{K,t_j}}\bigl\|\widehat s_{t_j}(U)-\nabla\log q_{K,t_j}(U)\bigr\|_\Lambda^2
 \le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\Lambda}^2,
\]
where $\|z\|_\Lambda^2:=z^\top\Lambda z$.
head: environment
name: Score accuracy

label: ass:girsanov
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:girsanov}
The change of measure between the exact reverse process and the sampler is
valid, i.e.\ the corresponding stochastic exponential is a true martingale.
This holds, for instance, when the score estimates grow at most linearly,
which can be enforced by clipping, and for exact Gaussian scores
(Appendix~\ref{app:general-rates}).

label: thm:end-to-end
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:end-to-end}
Let $q=\mathcal{N}(0,C)$ with the exact power law \eqref{eq:powerlaw2}, let $\eta>0$
and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, and let the sampler use the exact scores
$\widehat s_{t_j}=\nabla\log q_{K,t_j}$. Set
\[
 K:=K_\varepsilon(\eta),
 \qquad
 \sigma^2:=C_{\mathrm{sp}}K^{-\beta},
\]
\[
 T:=\frac2{\lambda_0}\log\frac{4\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}}{\sigma\varepsilon},
\]
assume $K<d$, and use a uniform grid with
\[
 N\ \ge\ c\,\max\Bigl\{
 \frac{\lambda_0^2T^2K}{\varepsilon^2},\
 \frac{\lambda_0^{3/2}T^{3/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}}{\sigma\,\varepsilon},\
 \lambda_0T
 \Bigr\}
\]
for an absolute constant $c$. Then the truncated sampler satisfies
$\mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p^\eta,q^\eta)\le\varepsilon$, with
\[
 N=\widetilde O\bigl(\varepsilon^{-4\beta/(2\beta-1)}\bigr),
\]
where $\widetilde O$ hides logarithmic factors and constants depending only
on $\lambda_0$, $C_{\mathrm{sp}}$, $\beta$ and $\eta$.
head: environment
name: End-to-end complexity

label: prop:full-bound
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:full-bound}
For any data law $q$ and any law $\nu_\perp$ on the discarded coordinates,
the output law $\widetilde p=p\otimes\nu_\perp$ satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p,q)\le\mathrm{TV}(p,q_K)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCA}},
\]
where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCA}}:=\mathrm{TV}(q_K\otimes\nu_\perp,\,q)$.
If $\nu_\perp$ is the true law $q_\perp$ of the discarded coordinates, then
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCA}}\le\sqrt{I/2}$, where $I$ is the mutual information
between the retained and the discarded coordinates.
head: environment
name: Truncation error for general data

label: prop:learnable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:learnable}
Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ satisfy $\mathbb{E} X=0$ and $\mathbb{E}\|X\|^2<\infty$, and write
$\sigma_i^2:=\mathbb{E} X_i^2$ for its coordinate variances in a fixed orthonormal
basis. For a noise level $\eta>0$ let $Y=X+\eta Z$ with
$Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_d)$ independent of $X$, and let $p_\eta:=\mathrm{Law}(Y)$ (the smoothed
law $q^\eta$ of \eqref{eq:smoothed-target} when $X\sim q$). Then, for every
coordinate $i$,
\[
 \partial_i\log p_\eta(y)
 =\underbrace{-\frac{y_i}{\eta^2}}_{\text{Gaussian reference}}
 +\underbrace{\frac{m_i(y)}{\eta^2}}_{\text{data-dependent correction}},
 \qquad
 m_i(y):=\mathbb{E}[X_i\mid Y=y],
\]
and, writing $g_i(\eta):=\sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2+\eta^2)$ for the Wiener gain,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:learnable-fraction}
 g_i(\eta)^2
 \;\le\;
 \frac{\mathbb{E}\,m_i(Y)^2}{\mathbb{E}\,Y_i^2}
 \;\le\;
 g_i(\eta).
\end{equation}
The lower bound is attained when $X$ is Gaussian with covariance diagonal in
the chosen basis.
head: environment
name: Correction to the Gaussian reference score

title: Proof
body_md:
The decomposition is Tweedie's formula
$\nabla\log p_\eta(y)=(\mathbb{E}[X\mid Y=y]-y)/\eta^2$, and
$\mathbb{E} Y_i^2=\sigma_i^2+\eta^2$ because $X$ and $Z$ are independent and centered.
Upper bound: by Jensen's inequality for conditional expectations,
$\mathbb{E}\,m_i(Y)^2\le\mathbb{E} X_i^2=\sigma_i^2$, so the ratio is at most
$\sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2+\eta^2)=g_i$.
Lower bound: by orthogonality of the conditional mean,
$\mathbb{E}\,m_i(Y)^2=\sigma_i^2-\mathbb{E}\bigl(X_i-m_i(Y)\bigr)^2$, and since the
conditional mean minimises the mean-squared error over all measurable
functions of $Y$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl(X_i-m_i(Y)\bigr)^2
 \le\mathbb{E}\bigl(X_i-g_iY_i\bigr)^2
 =\sigma_i^2-2g_i\sigma_i^2+g_i^2(\sigma_i^2+\eta^2)
 =\sigma_i^2(1-g_i).
\]
Hence $\mathbb{E}\,m_i(Y)^2\ge g_i\sigma_i^2$, and the ratio is at least
$g_i\sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2+\eta^2)=g_i^2$. If $X$ is Gaussian with diagonal
covariance, then $m_i(y)=g_iy_i$ and $\mathbb{E}\,m_i(Y)^2=g_i^2(\sigma_i^2+\eta^2)$,
which is the lower bound.

head: environment
name: Exact divergence of truncation

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Identity.} Since the two laws agree on the first $K$ coordinates and
are products, the divergence is the sum over $i>K$ of the divergences between
$\mathcal{N}(0,\eta^2)$ and $\mathcal{N}(0,\eta^2(1+x_i))$. The one-dimensional formula
$\mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(0,a)\|\mathcal{N}(0,b))=\frac12(a/b-1-\log(a/b))$ with $a/b=1/(1+x_i)=1-g_i$
gives $\frac12[\log(1+x_i)-x_i/(1+x_i)]=\frac12[-g_i-\log(1-g_i)]$.

\emph{Upper bound.} For $g\in[0,1)$,
\[
 -g-\log(1-g)=\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{g^k}{k}
 \le\frac{g^2}{2}\sum_{j\ge0}g^j
 =\frac{g^2}{2(1-g)}
 =\frac{x^2}{2(1+x)} .
\]

\emph{Lower bound in divergence.} Let $\phi(x)=\log(1+x)-x/(1+x)$. On
$[0,1]$ the function $\phi(x)-x^2/8$ vanishes at $0$ and has derivative
$x\bigl((1+x)^{-2}-\frac14\bigr)\ge0$, so $\phi(x)\ge x^2/8$ there; the outer
factor $\frac12$ gives the claim.

\emph{Upper bound in total variation.} Pinsker's inequality
$\mathrm{TV}\le\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}/2}$ and \eqref{eq:sharp-kl}.

\emph{Lower bound in total variation.} Let
$\mathrm{BC}(\mu,\nu)=\int\sqrt{\mathrm d\mu\,\mathrm d\nu}$ be the
Bhattacharyya coefficient. It is multiplicative over independent
coordinates, and $1-\mathrm{BC}(\mu,\nu)\le\mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu)$ (Le Cam's inequality
$H^2\le\mathrm{TV}$ with $H^2=1-\mathrm{BC}$). For centered one-dimensional Gaussians
with variances $a,b$, $\mathrm{BC}=\bigl(2\sqrt{ab}/(a+b)\bigr)^{1/2}$; with
$a=\eta^2$ and $b=\eta^2(1+x_i)$ this equals $1-\psi(x_i)$, where
\[
 \psi(x):=1-\Bigl(\frac{2\sqrt{1+x}}{2+x}\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
The function $\psi$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$, because the ratio of the
geometric to the arithmetic mean of $1$ and $1+x$ decreases in $x$. The ratio
$\psi(x)/x^2$ decreases on $(0,1]$ from its limit $1/16$ at $0$ to
$\psi(1)\approx0.0290>1/35$. Hence $\psi(x)\ge\min\{x^2,1\}/35$ for all
$x\ge0$, and
\[
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 \ge1-\prod_{i>K}\bigl(1-\psi(x_i)\bigr)
 \ge1-\exp\Bigl(-\sum_{i>K}\psi(x_i)\Bigr)
 \ge1-e^{-S/35}
 \ge\frac12\min\Bigl\{1,\frac{S}{35}\Bigr\},
\]
using $1-e^{-u}\ge\frac12\min\{u,1\}$ for $u\ge0$.

label: thm:tv-dim
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:tv-dim}
Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:lipschitz}, \ref{ass:second_moment}, \ref{ass:score_error},
\ref{ass:girsanov} and~\ref{ass:finite-kl} in $\mathbb{R}^r$, with the unweighted Fisher bound $\mathbb
E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}\|\nabla\log q_{r,t}(U)\|^2\le C_F^{(0)}r$ from
Lemma~\ref{lem:fisher} ($C_F^{(0)}=L$). We additionally assume that
the one-step score-perturbation bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:score-perturb}
applies uniformly to the coefficient-space marginals $q_{r,t}$,
$t\in[0,T]$ - that is, the differentiation-under-the-integral,
integration-by-parts, and conditional Brascamp-Lieb steps used in its
proof are valid for these marginals. This holds under standard
smoothness and tail-decay conditions and is the only regularity used
beyond Assumption~\ref{ass:lipschitz}. If $\delta\le\min\{\tfrac18,
\tfrac{1}{128L\sigma^2}\}$
then, writing
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}^2 := \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{N}
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t_j}}\left\|\widehat s_{t_j}(U)-\nabla\log q_{r,t_j}(U)\right\|^2,
\]
there is a universal constant $\widetilde C>0$ with
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{TV}(p_{\mathrm{out}},q_r) \le e^{-\lambda_{\min}T}\sqrt{\tfrac12\mathrm{KL}(q_r\|\gamma_r)}
+ \widetilde C\sigma\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}T}\Big(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}
+ Lm_{2,r}\delta + (1+L\sigma^2)\sqrt{C_F^{(0)}r}\,\delta + L\sigma\sqrt{r\delta}\Big)
\end{equation*}
where $\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}$ are the extreme rates of
$\Lambda$ and $m_{2,r}^2:=\mathbb E_{U\sim q_r}\|U\|^2$.

name: TV convergence, dimension-dependent warm-up

label: thm:tv-trace
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Trace-dependent TV convergence

label: cor:topK
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:topK}
Let \(V_K\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times K}\) be any matrix with orthonormal columns, and
let \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_K>0\) be any rates. Let
\(\kappa:=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}=\lambda_1/\lambda_K\) denote the
condition number. Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lipschitz}, \ref{ass:second_moment}, \ref{ass:score_error},
\ref{ass:girsanov} and~\ref{ass:finite-kl}, with the weighted Fisher bound
$\mathbb E\|\nabla\log q_{K,t}(U)\|_\Lambda^2\le C_F\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)$
furnished by Lemma~\ref{lem:fisher} ($C_F=L$), under the one-step
score-perturbation hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:tv-trace}, and under the small-step
condition
\begin{equation}
\delta\le\min\!\Bigl(
 \tfrac{1}{8},\,
 \tfrac{1}{128\sqrt{\kappa}\,L\sigma^2}
\Bigr),
\label{eq:small-step-cor1}
\end{equation}
there exists a constant \(C_0(\kappa)>0\), depending only on \(\kappa\) and
universal constants, such that
\begin{align}
\mathrm{TV}(p,q_K)
&\le
e^{-\lambda_K T}
\sqrt{\frac12\,\mathrm{KL}(q_K\|\gamma_K)}
\nonumber\\
&\quad+C_0(\kappa)\,\sigma\sqrt{T}\Bigl(
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\bm{\Lambda}}
 +L\delta\sqrt{\mathfrak{m}_{2,\bm{\Lambda}}^2
 +\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})}
 \nonumber\\
&\qquad\qquad
 +(1+L\sigma^2)\sqrt{C_F}\,\delta\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})}
 +L\sigma\sqrt{\delta\,\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})}
\Bigr),
\label{eq:tv-cor1}
\end{align}
where \(\lambda_K=\min_i\lambda_i\) is the smallest active rate,
\[
\mathfrak{m}_{2,\bm{\Lambda}}^2
=\sum_{i=1}^K\lambda_i\sigma_i^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})=\sum_{i=1}^K\lambda_i,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda}^2)=\sum_{i=1}^K\lambda_i^2.
\]
For non-PCA bases, the expression for \(\mathfrak m_{2,\bm{\Lambda}}^2\) should be
read as \(\mathbb E\|U_0\|_\Lambda^2\). The bound depends on \(K\) and the
rates \(\{\lambda_i\}_{i=1}^K\) only through these weighted trace quantities,
and is independent of the ambient dimension \(d\).
head: environment
name: Top-$K$ TV bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:tv-trace} with $r=K$, $q_r=q_K$ and
$\lambda_{\min}=\lambda_K$.
head: environment

label: prop:isotropic
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:isotropic}
Let $1\le K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$ and replace the Wiener-gain rates by the
constant rates $\lambda_i\equiv\lambda_0$, $i\le K$. Assume the hypotheses
of Corollary~\ref{cor:topK} for the resulting isotropic process, with
Lipschitz constant $L_{\mathrm{iso}}$ in Assumption~\ref{ass:lipschitz} and
score error $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\lambda_0I}$ in
Assumption~\ref{ass:score_error}. Then the bound \eqref{eq:tv-cor2} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} holds for the isotropic sampler with $L$
replaced by $L_{\mathrm{iso}}$, $\kappa_0$ replaced by $1$, and the mixing
factor $e^{-\lambda_\star T}$ replaced by $e^{-\lambda_0T}$.
Consequently the step count $N=\widetilde O(K/\varepsilon^2)$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} also holds for isotropic diffusion on the same
subspace. Moreover, the weighted norms of the
two schemes are equivalent on the retained subspace:
$\lambda_\star\|z\|^2\le\|z\|_{\Lambda}^2\le\lambda_0\|z\|^2$ for the
Wiener-gain matrix $\Lambda$; for a fixed error vector and a fixed
evaluation distribution the two error norms therefore differ by at most the
factor $\kappa_0$. This does not compare how hard the two score
functions are to learn: the two processes have different forward marginals and
different target scores. For Gaussian data with the exact
power law, $L_{\mathrm{iso}}=L=\sigma^{-2}$.
head: environment
name: Isotropic rates on the same retained subspace

title: Proof
body_md:
With $\lambda_i\equiv\lambda_0$ we have $\kappa=1$, $\lambda_K=\lambda_0$,
$\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)=\lambda_0K$, and
$m_{2,\Lambda}^2=\lambda_0\sum_{i\le K}\sigma_i^2\le\lambda_0C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)$
by the upper power-law envelope. These are the bounds of
Lemma~\ref{lem:traces}, so substituting them into Corollary~\ref{cor:topK}
gives \eqref{eq:tv-cor2} with the stated replacements, and the step-count
calculation in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} is unchanged. The norm
equivalence follows from $\lambda_\star\le\lambda_i\le\lambda_0$ for the
Wiener-gain rates on $i\le K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$. For Gaussian data the
isotropic marginal covariance has diagonal entries
$e^{-2\lambda_0t}\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2(1-e^{-2\lambda_0t})\ge\sigma^2$, since
$\sigma_i^2\ge\sigma^2$ for $i\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$, so the score is
$\sigma^{-2}$-Lipschitz as in the Wiener-gain case.
head: environment

label: lem:traces
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:traces}
Under the upper side of Assumption~\ref{ass:powerlaw}, namely
$\sigma_i^2\le C_{\mathrm{sp}}i^{-\beta}$ with $\beta>1$, use the Wiener-gain
rates~\eqref{eq:wiener-rates} and let
$1\le K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$. Then
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)
 &\le \lambda_0K,
 \label{eq:trL}\\[3pt]
 \operatorname{tr}(\Lambda^2)
 &\le \lambda_0^2K,
 \label{eq:trL2}\\[3pt]
 m_{2,\Lambda}^2
 &\le \lambda_0C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta),
 \label{eq:m2L}
\end{align}
where $\zeta(\beta)=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}i^{-\beta}<\infty$. In particular,
the bounds do not depend on the ambient dimension $d$.
head: environment
name: Trace bounds under Wiener-gain rates and power-law decay

title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout, write
\[
 g_i := \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2}\in[0,1)
\]
for the Wiener gain.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Bounding \(\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)\).}

Since \(\lambda_i=\lambda_0g_i\) and \(0\le g_i\le1\),
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)
 =
 \lambda_0\sum_{i=1}^K g_i
 \le
 \lambda_0 K.
\]

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Bounding \(\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda^2)\).}

Since \(0\le g_i\le1\), we have \(g_i^2\le g_i\le1\). Hence
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\Lambda^2)
 =
 \lambda_0^2\sum_{i=1}^K g_i^2
 \le
 \lambda_0^2 K.
\]

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Bounding \(m_{2,\Lambda}^2\).}

By definition,
\[
 m_{2,\Lambda}^2
 =
 \sum_{i=1}^K \lambda_i\sigma_i^2
 =
 \lambda_0\sum_{i=1}^K g_i\sigma_i^2.
\]
Since \(g_i\le1\),
\[
 m_{2,\Lambda}^2
 \le
 \lambda_0\sum_{i=1}^K\sigma_i^2.
\]
Using the upper power-law bound \(\sigma_i^2\le C_{\mathrm{sp}} i^{-\beta}\),
\[
 m_{2,\Lambda}^2
 \le
 \lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\sum_{i=1}^{K}i^{-\beta}
 \le
 \lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}i^{-\beta}
 =
 \lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta).
\]
Since \(\beta>1\), the zeta sum is finite. Therefore
\[
 m_{2,\Lambda}^2
 \le
 \lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta),
\]
independently of \(K\) and \(d\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Rates.} Since $K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}\le(C_{\mathrm{sp}}/\sigma^2)^{1/\beta}$,
the lower envelope gives, for every $i\le K$,
$\sigma_i^2\ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}i^{-\beta}\ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}K^{-\beta}
\ge(c_{\mathrm{sp}}/C_{\mathrm{sp}})\sigma^2$, and therefore
\[
 \lambda_i\ge\lambda_0\,\frac{c_{\mathrm{sp}}}{c_{\mathrm{sp}}+C_{\mathrm{sp}}}
 =\lambda_\star,
 \qquad
 \kappa\le\frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda_\star}=\kappa_0 .
\]

\emph{Bound.} Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:topK}. Its mixing term is at most
$e^{-\lambda_\star T}\sqrt{\frac12\mathrm{KL}(q_K\|\gamma_K)}$ because
$\lambda_K\ge\lambda_\star$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:fisher}, $C_F=L$. Substituting
the trace bounds of Lemma~\ref{lem:traces} and absorbing $C_0(\kappa)\le
C_0(\kappa_0)$, which uses that $C_0$ is nondecreasing in $\kappa$ (one can
take $C_0(\kappa)=c\sqrt\kappa$), into a constant $C'$ depending only on
$\beta$ and $\kappa_0$ gives \eqref{eq:tv-cor2}.

\emph{Step count.} The choice of $T$ makes the mixing term at most
$\varepsilon/2$, and the assumption on $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\Lambda}$
makes the score term at most a small constant times $\varepsilon$. On a
uniform grid, $\delta\le\lambda_{\max}T/N\le\lambda_0T/N$. The largest of the
three discretisation terms for small $\delta$ is
$C'\sigma\sqrt T\,L\sigma\sqrt{\lambda_0\delta K}$, which is at most a small
constant times $\varepsilon$ once
$\delta\lesssim\varepsilon^2/(\sigma^4TL^2\lambda_0K)$, i.e.\ once
\[
 N\gtrsim\frac{(L\sigma^2)^2\lambda_0^2T^2K}{\varepsilon^2}.
\]
The two remaining discretisation terms are linear in $\delta$ and are smaller
under the same choice for small $\varepsilon$, and the small-step condition
\eqref{eq:small-step-cor2} holds once
$N\ge\lambda_0T\max\{8,\,128\sqrt{\kappa_0}\,L\sigma^2\}$.
Since $T$ is logarithmic in $1/\varepsilon$, this is
$N=\widetilde O(K/\varepsilon^2)$.

label: lem:active-sigma
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: $\sigma$-explicit active error, Gaussian case

title: Proof
body_md:
We first collect the constants. For $i\le K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$ the
exact power law gives $\sigma_i^2\ge\sigma^2$, hence $g_i(\sigma)\ge1/2$,
$\lambda_i\in[\lambda_0/2,\lambda_0]$ and $\kappa\le2$. The marginal
$q_{K,t}$ is $\mathcal{N}(0,D_t)$ with diagonal entries
$e^{-2\lambda_it}\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2(1-e^{-2\lambda_it})\ge\sigma^2$, so its
score $-D_t^{-1}u$ is $\sigma^{-2}$-Lipschitz: $L=C_F=\sigma^{-2}$ and
$L\sigma^2=1$. Exact scores give $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\Lambda}=0$;
they are linear, so Assumption~\ref{ass:girsanov} holds by the linear-growth
criterion of Appendix~\ref{app:general-rates}, and Gaussian marginals satisfy
the tail and regularity conditions. Lemma~\ref{lem:traces} gives
$\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)\le\lambda_0K$ and
$m_{2,\Lambda}^2\le\lambda_0C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)$. Finally, with
$\mu_i=\sigma_i^2/\sigma^2\ge1$,
$\mathrm{KL}(q_K\|\gamma_K)=\frac12\sum_{i\le K}(\mu_i-1-\log\mu_i)
\le\frac12\sum_{i\le K}\mu_i\le C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)/(2\sigma^2)$. On a uniform
grid $\delta\le\lambda_{\max}T/N\le\lambda_0T/N\le1/(128\sqrt2)$, so the
small-step condition of Corollary~\ref{cor:topK} (with $\kappa\le2$ and
$L\sigma^2=1$) and $\lambda_{\max}\Delta\tau_{\max}\le1$ hold. Substituting
into \eqref{eq:tv-cor1}, the mixing term is at most
$e^{-\lambda_0T/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}/(2\sigma)$, and the
three discretisation terms are bounded as follows:
\begin{align*}
 \sigma\sqrt T\,L\delta\sqrt{m_{2,\Lambda}^2+\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)}
 &\le\lambda_0^{3/2}T^{3/2}\Bigl(\frac{\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}}
  {\sigma N}+\frac{\sqrt K}{N}\Bigr),\\
 \sigma\sqrt T\,(1+L\sigma^2)\sqrt{C_F}\,\delta\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)}
 &\le2\lambda_0^{3/2}T^{3/2}\frac{\sqrt K}{N},\\
 \sigma\sqrt T\,L\sigma\sqrt{\delta\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda)}
 &\le\lambda_0T\sqrt{\frac KN},
\end{align*}
using $\sqrt{a+b}\le\sqrt a+\sqrt b$. Collecting terms gives the claim.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:error-decomposition}, it suffices to make the truncation error
and the sampling error each at most $\varepsilon/2$.

\emph{Truncation error.} With $K=K_\varepsilon(\eta)<d$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:num-directions}(a) gives
$\mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta)\le\varepsilon/2$.

\emph{Admissibility of $K$.} With $\sigma^2=C_{\mathrm{sp}}K^{-\beta}$ we have
$(C_{\mathrm{sp}}/\sigma^2)^{1/\beta}=K$, so $d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}=K$
(using $K<d$) and Lemma~\ref{lem:active-sigma} applies.

\emph{Sampling error.} We require each of the four terms of
Lemma~\ref{lem:active-sigma} to be at most $\varepsilon/8$. The mixing term
is at most $\varepsilon/8$ by the choice of $T$, since
$e^{-\lambda_0T/2}=\sigma\varepsilon/(4\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)})$. The
three discretisation terms are at most $\varepsilon/8$ once
$N\ge64C_0^2\lambda_0^2T^2K/\varepsilon^2$,
$N\ge24C_0\lambda_0^{3/2}T^{3/2}\sqrt K/\varepsilon$ and
$N\ge8C_0\lambda_0^{3/2}T^{3/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}/(\sigma\varepsilon)$,
and the step-size condition of the lemma holds once
$N\ge128\sqrt2\,\lambda_0T$. Because $\sigma^2\le C_{\mathrm{sp}}\le
C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)$ and $\varepsilon<1$, we have $\lambda_0T\ge1$, and
then the second requirement is implied by the first. This gives the
condition on $N$ in the theorem.

\emph{Order of $N$.} We have $1/\sigma=K^{\beta/2}/\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}$ and
$K=K_\varepsilon(\eta)\asymp\varepsilon^{-2/(2\beta-1)}$, so
\[
 \frac{K}{\varepsilon^2}\asymp\varepsilon^{-\frac{4\beta}{2\beta-1}},
 \qquad
 \frac{K^{\beta/2}}{\varepsilon}\asymp\varepsilon^{-\frac{3\beta-1}{2\beta-1}},
\]
and $3\beta-1<4\beta$, so the first term dominates; $T=O(\lambda_0^{-1}
\log(1/\varepsilon))$ contributes only logarithmic factors.

title: Proof
body_md:
The sampler outputs
$\tilde{X} = V_K\hat{X} + Z$ with $\hat{X} \sim p$ and
$Z \sim \nu_\perp$ independent, supported on the orthogonal
subspaces $S_K$ and $S_K^\perp$ respectively. The law of
$\tilde{X}$ is $\tilde{p} = p \otimes \nu_\perp$ (product on
$S_K \times S_K^\perp \cong \mathbb{R}^d$).

\begin{align}
 \mathrm{TV}(\tilde{p},\,q)
 &= \mathrm{TV}(p\otimes\nu_\perp,\;q) \notag\\
 &\le \mathrm{TV}(p\otimes\nu_\perp,\;q_K\otimes\nu_\perp)
 + \mathrm{TV}(q_K\otimes\nu_\perp,\;q).
 \label{eq:app-triangle}
\end{align}

The distributions $p\otimes\nu_\perp$ and $q_K\otimes\nu_\perp$ share
the factor $\nu_\perp$. We claim:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:app-product-tv}
 \mathrm{TV}(\mu_1\otimes\nu,\;\mu_2\otimes\nu)
 = \mathrm{TV}(\mu_1,\,\mu_2)
\end{equation}
for any probability measures $\mu_1,\mu_2$ and any probability measure $\nu$.
Indeed, let $\Delta:=\mu_1-\mu_2$ be the signed measure difference. Since
$\nu$ is a positive probability measure, the variation measure factorizes:
\[
 |\Delta\otimes\nu|=|\Delta|\otimes\nu .
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathrm{TV}(\mu_1\otimes\nu,\mu_2\otimes\nu)
 &=\frac12 |(\mu_1-\mu_2)\otimes\nu|(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\\
 &=\frac12 |\mu_1-\mu_2|(\mathcal X)\,\nu(\mathcal Y)\\
 &=\mathrm{TV}(\mu_1,\mu_2),
\end{aligned}
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:app-product-tv}.

Applying~\eqref{eq:app-product-tv} with $\mu_1 = p$,
$\mu_2 = q_K$, $\nu = \nu_\perp$ to the first term
of~\eqref{eq:app-triangle}:
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(p\otimes\nu_\perp,\;q_K\otimes\nu_\perp)
 = \mathrm{TV}(p,\,q_K).
\]
Substituting into~\eqref{eq:app-triangle} and using the
definition of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCA}}$:
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(\tilde{p},\,q)
 \le \mathrm{TV}(p,\,q_K) + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCA}}.
\]

title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:iid-patches}
The \(n_{\mathrm{patch}}\) patches
\(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(n_{\mathrm{patch}})}\) used to form the empirical covariance
\(\widehat\Sigma\) are drawn independently from the population patch marginal

head: environment
name: Independent patch sampling

label: thm:empirical
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:empirical}
Assume Assumption~\ref{ass:iid-patches}, use Wiener-gain rates, and assume
\[
 q=\mathcal N(0,\mathcal C),
 \qquad
 \mathcal C=V\mathrm{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_d^2)V^\top,
 \qquad
 \sigma_i^2=C_{\mathrm{sp}}i^{-\beta},
\]
with \(C_{\mathrm{sp}}>0\) and \(\beta>1\). Let
\[
 V_K=[v_1,\ldots,v_K],
 \qquad
 P_K:=V_KV_K^\top
\]
be the population top-\(K\) eigenspace and projector. Let \(\widehat V_K\) be
the empirical top-\(K\) PCA basis estimated from \(n_{\mathrm{patch}}\) training
patches, and define
\[
 \widehat P_K:=\widehat V_K\widehat V_K^\top.
\]
Let
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i
 =
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\widehat\sigma_i^2}{\widehat\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2},
 \qquad
 \widehat\Lambda:=\mathrm{diag}(\widehat\lambda_1,\ldots,\widehat\lambda_K).
\]
Assume $1\le K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$ and that the covariance
concentration event
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \Delta_n
\]
holds, where \(\Sigma\) is the population patch covariance and
\(\widehat\Sigma\) is the empirical patch covariance. Suppose further that
\[
 \Delta_n
 \le
 c_0
 \min\left\{
  \sigma^2,\,
  \sigma_K^2,\,
  \delta_{\mathrm{gap}},\,
  \frac{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}
 \right\},
\]
for a sufficiently small universal constant \(c_0>0\), where
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{gap}}:=\sigma_K^2-\sigma_{K+1}^2.
\]

In the empirical active coordinates, the true projected covariance is generally
non-diagonal:
\[
 \widehat C_K:=\widehat V_K^\top\mathcal C\,\widehat V_K.
\]
Let \(\widehat q_{K,t}\) denote the Gaussian marginal of the empirical
active-space OU process with initial covariance \(\widehat C_K\) and rate matrix
\(\widehat\Lambda\), namely
\[
 \widehat q_{K,t}
 =
 \mathcal N(0,\widehat D_t),
 \qquad
 \widehat D_t
 =
 e^{-\widehat\Lambda t}\widehat C_K e^{-\widehat\Lambda t}
 +
 \sigma^2(I_K-e^{-2\widehat\Lambda t}).
\]
Assume that the empirical active-space score is oracle-exact (note that
$\widehat D_t$ involves the unknown population covariance $\mathcal C$, so this
is an oracle assumption, not a data-derived score):
\[
 \widehat s_t(u)=\nabla\log \widehat q_{K,t}(u)
 =
 -\widehat D_t^{-1}u.
\]

Then, with the same probability as the covariance concentration event,
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta,\,q^\eta)
 \le
 \underbrace{
 \widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac K N}\right)
 }_{\mathrm{(I)}\ \mathrm{sampling}}
 +
 \underbrace{
 C_1
 \frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\eta^2\,\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}
 \Delta_n
 }_{\mathrm{(II)}\ \mathrm{basis/covariance\ mismatch}}
 +
 \underbrace{
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 }_{\mathrm{(III)}\ \mathrm{truncation}},
\]
where \(C_1>0\) is independent of the ambient dimension \(d\), and
(III) is the truncation error of Section~\ref{sec:sharp}, bounded by
Theorem~\ref{thm:num-directions}(a). The hidden
constants in the \(\widetilde O(\cdot)\) term may depend on fixed model
parameters such as \((\lambda_0,\sigma,\eta,\beta,T,m_2)\), but not on \(d\).
The small-perturbation conditions imply that the empirical Gaussian marginals
also satisfy the coefficient-space Lipschitz-score and weighted Fisher
assumptions with constants independent of \(d\). The sampling term is applied
to the empirical OU process itself; no Girsanov comparison between the
population rate matrix \(\Lambda\) and the empirical rate matrix
\(\widehat\Lambda\) is used.

label: thm:decouple
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:decouple}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $K_{\max}=d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$. Under
Assumption~\ref{ass:sufficient_data}, the basis-estimation term of
Theorem~\ref{thm:empirical} is at most $\varepsilon/4$ uniformly over
$K\le K_{\max}$, so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:reduced}
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 \le
 \widetilde O\Bigl(\sqrt{\tfrac KN}\Bigr)
 +\mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr)
 +\frac{\varepsilon}{4}.
\end{equation}
For a fixed diffusion noise level $\sigma$, any choice of $K\le K_{\max}$ and
$N$ that makes the population bound at most $3\varepsilon/4$ therefore gives
error at most $\varepsilon$ with the estimated basis and rates. The required
number of patches depends on $d$, the spectrum, $\sigma$, $\eta$ and
$\varepsilon$, but not on $N$.

label: prop:gmm-lift
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:gmm-lift}
Let $q_{\mathrm{GMM}}^\eta=\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_mq_m^\eta$ and
$p_{\mathrm{GMM}}^\eta=\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_mp_m^\eta$. If
$\mathrm{TV}(p_m^\eta,q_m^\eta)\le\varepsilon_m$ for all components, then
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(p_{\mathrm{GMM}}^\eta,q_{\mathrm{GMM}}^\eta)
 \le\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_m\varepsilon_m.
\]
Here $p_m^\eta$ is a truncated sampler adapted to component $m$, run with
probability $\pi_m$.
head: environment
name: Mixture lifting of the Gaussian bound

title: Proof
body_md:
The convexity of the total variation gives
\[
 \mathrm{TV}\!\left(\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_mp_m^\eta,
    \sum_{m=1}^M\pi_mq_m^\eta\right)
 \le\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_m\mathrm{TV}(p_m^\eta,q_m^\eta)
 \le\sum_{m=1}^M\pi_m\varepsilon_m.
\]

label: lem:tv-dp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tv-dp}
Let $\mu,\nu$ be probability measures on a measurable space
$(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ and let $\Phi:\Omega\to S$ be measurable.
Then
\[
\mathrm{TV}(\Phi_\#\mu,\Phi_\#\nu)\le \mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu).
\]
head: environment
name: Data processing for TV

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition,
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{TV}(\Phi_\# \mu, \Phi_\# \nu)
&= \sup_{A\subseteq S} \bigl| (\Phi_\# \mu)(A) - (\Phi_\# \nu)(A) \bigr| \\
&= \sup_{A\subseteq S} \bigl| \mu(\Phi^{-1}(A)) - \nu(\Phi^{-1}(A)) \bigr| \\
&\le \sup_{B\subseteq \Omega} \bigl| \mu(B) - \nu(B) \bigr| \\
&= \mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu).
\end{align*}

label: lem:moment
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moment}
For the forward OU \eqref{eq:generic-forward-OU} on $\mathbb{R}^r$,
\[
\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}\left\|U_\tau\right\|^2 \le m_{2,r}^2 + r\sigma^2.
\]
head: environment
name: Forward second moment bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Solve \eqref{eq:generic-forward-OU} explicitly:
\[
U_\tau = e^{-\bm{\Lambda}\tau}U_0
 + \int_0^\tau e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s.
\]
Then:
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
= \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|e^{-\bm{\Lambda}\tau}U_0\right\|^2\right]
+ \mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_0^\tau e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s\Big\|^2\right].
\]
The cross term vanishes because the stochastic integral has zero
mean and is independent of $U_0$.
For the first term, $\|e^{-\bm{\Lambda}\tau}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1$,
so $\mathbb{E}\left\|e^{-\bm{\Lambda}\tau}U_0\right\|^2\le \mathbb{E}\left\|U_0\right\|^2$.
For the second term, by It\^{o}'s isometry:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_0^\tau e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s\Big\|^2\right]
&= \int_0^\tau \operatorname{tr}\!\Bigl(e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}(2\bm{\Lambda}\sigma^2)
 e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}\Bigr)\,ds.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\int_0^\tau \operatorname{tr}\!\Bigl(e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}(2\bm{\Lambda}\sigma^2)
e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(\tau-s)}\Bigr)\,ds
&= \sum_{i=1}^r \int_0^\tau 2\lambda_i\sigma^2 e^{-2\lambda_i(\tau-s)}\,ds \\
&= \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma^2\!\left(1 - e^{-2\lambda_i\tau}\right) \\
&\le \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma^2 = r\sigma^2.
\end{align*}
Finally, $\mathbb{E}\left\|U_0\right\|^2 = m_{2,r}^2$ by definition.
Combining gives $\sup_{\tau}\mathbb{E}\left\|U_\tau\right\|^2\le m_{2,r}^2+r\sigma^2$.

label: lem:fisher
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fisher}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:lipschitz} (applied to the coefficient-space
marginals $q_{r,t}$ on $\mathbb{R}^r$), for every $t \in [\tau_0, T]$ and every
diagonal positive semidefinite matrix
$M = \mathrm{diag}(m_1, \dots, m_r)$, $m_i \ge 0$,
\[
  \mathbb{E}_{U \sim q_{r,t}}\bigl[\|\nabla \log q_{r,t}(U)\|_M^2\bigr]
  \le L \,\mathrm{tr}(M).
\]
In particular, for $M = I_r$,
$\mathbb{E}_{U \sim q_{r,t}}\bigl[\|\nabla \log q_{r,t}(U)\|^2\bigr] \le L r$.
head: environment
name: Fisher bound from score regularity

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $q_{r,t}=e^{-V_t}$ for some $V_t\in C^2(\mathbb R^r)$, as
guaranteed by Assumption~\ref{ass:lipschitz}. Fix a coordinate
\(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\). Since \(q_{r,t}=e^{-V_t}\), we have
\[
 \partial_i q_{r,t}(x)
 =
 -q_{r,t}(x)\,\partial_i V_t(x).
\]
Therefore
\[
 \partial_i\!\left(q_{r,t}\,\partial_i V_t\right)
 =
 (\partial_i q_{r,t})\,\partial_i V_t
 +
 q_{r,t}\,\partial_{ii}^2 V_t
 =
 -q_{r,t}(\partial_i V_t)^2
 +
 q_{r,t}\,\partial_{ii}^2 V_t.
\]
Rearranging gives the pointwise identity
\[
 q_{r,t}(\partial_i V_t)^2
 =
 q_{r,t}\,\partial_{ii}^2 V_t
 -
 \partial_i\!\left(q_{r,t}\,\partial_i V_t\right).
\]

Integrating over the cube \(Q_R=[-R,R]^r\) and applying the divergence theorem,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \int_{Q_R} q_{r,t}(x)(\partial_i V_t(x))^2\,dx
 &=
 \int_{Q_R} q_{r,t}(x)\,\partial_{ii}^2 V_t(x)\,dx \\
 &\quad
 -
 \int_{\partial Q_R}
 q_{r,t}(x)\,\partial_i V_t(x)\,n_i(x)\,dS(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the boundary condition in Assumption~\ref{ass:lipschitz}, the
boundary term converges to zero as \(R\to\infty\).

Since the score is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(V_t\in C^2\), we have
\[
 \|\nabla^2 V_t(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\]
and hence, for every \(i\),
\[
 \partial_{ii}^2 V_t(x)\le L.
\]
Moreover \(|\partial_{ii}^2 V_t(x)|\le L\), so dominated convergence applies to
the term
\[
 \int_{Q_R} q_{r,t}(x)\,\partial_{ii}^2V_t(x)\,dx,
\]
while the left-hand side converges by monotone convergence, its integrand
being nonnegative.
Letting \(R\to\infty\), we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  (\partial_i V_t(U))^2
 \right]
 =
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  \partial_{ii}^2 V_t(U)
 \right]
 \le
 L.
\]

Since
\[
 \nabla\log q_{r,t} = -\nabla V_t,
\]
we have
\[
 (\partial_i\log q_{r,t})^2
 =
 (\partial_i V_t)^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  (\partial_i\log q_{r,t}(U))^2
 \right]
 \le
 L.
\]

Multiplying by \(m_i\ge0\) and summing over \(i=1,\ldots,r\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  \|\nabla\log q_{r,t}(U)\|_M^2
 \right]
 &=
 \sum_{i=1}^r
 m_i\,
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  (\partial_i\log q_{r,t}(U))^2
 \right] \\
 &\le
 \sum_{i=1}^r
 m_i L
 =
 L\,\operatorname{tr}(M).
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(M=I_r\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{U\sim q_{r,t}}
 \left[
  \|\nabla\log q_{r,t}(U)\|^2
 \right]
 \le
 Lr.
\]
This completes the proof.

label: lem:move-forward
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:move-forward}
Let $0\le\tau<\tau'\le T$ and set $\Delta:=\tau'-\tau$. Then
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
\le 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2\!\left(\mathbb{E}[\|U_\tau\|^2]+r\sigma^2\right)
+ 4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta.
\]
In particular, using Lemma~\ref{lem:moment} and
$\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\le r\lambda_{\max}$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
\le 4\Bigl(\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2(m_{2,r}^2+2r\sigma^2)
 +\sigma^2 r\lambda_{\max}\Delta\Bigr).
\]
head: environment
name: Forward movement bound

title: Proof
body_md:
\[
U_{\tau'}-U_\tau
= \int_\tau^{\tau'}(-\bm{\Lambda} U_s)\,ds
+ \int_\tau^{\tau'}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s.
\]
Since $(a+b)^2\le 2a^2+2b^2$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
\le 2\mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds\Big\|^2\right]
+2\mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s\Big\|^2\right].
\]
By Cauchy-Schwarz and Jensen:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds\Big\|^2\right]
&= \mathbb{E}\left[\left\langle\int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds,
 \int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds\right\rangle\right] \\
&\le \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_\tau^{\tau'}\left\|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\right\|\,ds\right)^2\right] \\
&\le \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_\tau^{\tau'}1\,ds\right)
 \left(\int_\tau^{\tau'}\left\|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\right\|^2\,ds\right)\right] \\
&= \Delta\int_\tau^{\tau'}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\right\|^2\right]ds.
\end{align*}
By It\^{o}'s isometry:
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\Big\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_s\Big\|^2\right]
= \int_\tau^{\tau'}\operatorname{tr}(2\bm{\Lambda}\sigma^2)\,ds
= 2\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta.
\]
Therefore:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
&\le 2\Delta\int_\tau^{\tau'}\lambda_{\max}^2\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|U_s\right\|^2\right]ds
+4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta \\
&= 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta\int_\tau^{\tau'}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|U_s\right\|^2\right]ds
+4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta.
\end{align*}
From the OU explicit solution:
\[
U_s = e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(s-\tau)}U_\tau
+\int_\tau^s e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(s-r)}\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,\sigma\,dB_r,
\]
so
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[\|U_s\|^2]
&\le \mathbb{E}[\|e^{-\bm{\Lambda}(s-\tau)}U_\tau\|^2]
 +\sigma^2\sum_{i=1}^r(1-e^{-2\lambda_i(s-\tau)}) \\
&\le \mathbb{E}[\|U_\tau\|^2]+r\sigma^2.
\end{align*}
Substituting:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
&\le 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta\int_\tau^{\tau'}
 \!\left(\mathbb{E}[\|U_\tau\|^2]+r\sigma^2\right)ds
+4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta \\
&= 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2\!\left(\mathbb{E}[\|U_\tau\|^2]+r\sigma^2\right)
+4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta.
\end{align*}
From Lemma~\ref{lem:moment}:
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
\le 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2\!\left(m_{2,r}^2+2r\sigma^2\right)
+4\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\Delta.
\]
Since $\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\le r\lambda_{\max}$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\right\|^2\right]
\le 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2\!\left(m_{2,r}^2+2r\sigma^2\right)
+4\sigma^2 r\lambda_{\max}\Delta.
\]

label: eq:split-weighted
title: Proof
body_md:
From the SDE
$dU_t=-\bm{\Lambda} U_t\,dt+\sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,dB_t$,
the increment satisfies
\[
U_{\tau'}-U_\tau
=\int_\tau^{\tau'}(-\bm{\Lambda} U_s)\,ds
+\int_\tau^{\tau'}\sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,dB_s.
\]
By $(a+b)^2\le 2(a^2+b^2)$ applied in the
$\bm{\Lambda}$-norm:
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
\le 2\,\mathbb{E}\!\left\|
 \int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds
 \right\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
+2\,\mathbb{E}\!\left\|
 \int_\tau^{\tau'}\sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,dB_s
 \right\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}.
\label{eq:split-weighted}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{Drift term.}
By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality:
\[
\left\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}\bm{\Lambda} U_s\,ds
\right\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
\le\Delta\int_\tau^{\tau'}
 \|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}\,ds.
\]
Now:
\[
\|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
=\sum_i\lambda_i(\lambda_i U_{s,i})^2
=\sum_i\lambda_i^3 U_{s,i}^2
\le\lambda_{\max}\sum_i\lambda_i^2 U_{s,i}^2
=\lambda_{\max}\|\bm{\Lambda}^{1/2}U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}.
\]
Since $\|\bm{\Lambda}^{1/2}U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
=\sum_i\lambda_i\cdot\lambda_i U_{s,i}^2
=\|U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}^2}
\le\lambda_{\max}\|U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}$,
we have:
\[
\|\bm{\Lambda} U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
\le\lambda_{\max}^2\|U_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}.
\]
Therefore:
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left\|\int_{\tau}^{\tau'} \Lambda U_s\,ds\right\|^2_\Lambda
\;\leq\;
\lambda_{\max}^2 \Delta^2
\Bigl(m_{2,\Lambda}^2 + \sigma^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Lambda)\Bigr),
\label{eq:drift-weighted}
\end{equation}
here we used the pointwise bound
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb{E}\|U_s\|^2_\Lambda
 \;=\; \sum_i \lambda_i\,\mathbb{E}[U_{s,i}^2]
 \;=\; \sum_i \lambda_i
   \Bigl[e^{-2\lambda_i s}\mathbb{E}[U_{0,i}^2]
    + \sigma^2(1 - e^{-2\lambda_i s})\Bigr]
 \;\leq\; \sum_i \lambda_i\,\mathbb{E}[U_{0,i}^2]
   + \sigma^2\sum_i \lambda_i
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ou-second-moment-lambda}
 \;=\; m_{2,\Lambda}^2 + \sigma^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Lambda),
\end{equation}
which follows from the explicit OU marginal
$\mathbb{E}[U_{s,i}^2] = e^{-2\lambda_i s}\mathbb{E}[U_{0,i}^2]
+ \sigma^2(1-e^{-2\lambda_i s})$ by multiplying by $\lambda_i$ and summing;
the bound holds for all $s \geq 0$ and requires no knowledge of $T$.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{Noise term.}
By It\^o's isometry in the $\bm{\Lambda}$-norm:
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\!\left\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}
 \sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\,dB_s
 \right\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
&=\int_\tau^{\tau'}
 \operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(\bm{\Lambda}\cdot
 \sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}\cdot
 (\sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}})^\top\bigr)\,ds
\nonumber\\
&=\int_\tau^{\tau'}
 \operatorname{tr}(2\sigma^2\bm{\Lambda}^2)\,ds
\nonumber\\
&=2\sigma^2\Delta\,\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda}^2).
\label{eq:noise-weighted}
\end{align}
Here we used that for a diagonal diffusion
coefficient $G=\sigma\sqrt{2\bm{\Lambda}}$,
the It\^o isometry gives
$\mathbb{E}\|\int_\tau^{\tau'}G\,dB_s\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
=\int_\tau^{\tau'}\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda} GG^\top)\,ds
=\int_\tau^{\tau'}\operatorname{tr}(2\sigma^2\bm{\Lambda}^2)\,ds$,
since $\bm{\Lambda} GG^\top
=\bm{\Lambda}\cdot 2\sigma^2\bm{\Lambda}=2\sigma^2\bm{\Lambda}^2$.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{Combining.}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:drift-weighted}
and~\eqref{eq:noise-weighted}
into~\eqref{eq:split-weighted} gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
 \le
 2\lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2
 \bigl(m_{2,\bm{\Lambda}}^2+\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\bigr)
 +
 4\sigma^2\Delta\,\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda}^2).
\]
Loosening constants yields the stated bound
\[
 \mathbb{E}\|U_{\tau'}-U_\tau\|^2_{\bm{\Lambda}}
 \le
 4\Bigl[
  \lambda_{\max}^2\Delta^2
  \bigl(m_{2,\bm{\Lambda}}^2+\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda})\bigr)
  +
  \sigma^2\Delta\,\operatorname{tr}(\bm{\Lambda}^2)
 \Bigr].
\]

label: lem:score-perturb
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:score-perturb}
Let $Y\sim q$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a strictly positive $C^2$ density and
$L$-Lipschitz score $s(y):=\nabla\log q(y)$. Assume that the differentiations
under the integral sign, integrations by parts, and conditional Brascamp-Lieb
steps used below are justified; for instance, this holds under standard
smoothness and tail-decay conditions ensuring that the required boundary terms
vanish.
Let $D=\mathrm{diag}(\rho_1,\dots,\rho_d)$ with
\[
\rho_i\in[1-\zeta,1),\qquad \zeta\in(0,1/2].
\]
Define
\[
\Sigma:=\sigma^2(I-D^2),
\qquad
Y':=DY,
\qquad
X:=Y'+\varepsilon,
\qquad
\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)
\ \text{independent of }Y.
\]
Let $\tilde q:=\mathrm{Law}(X)$ and $\tilde s(u):=\nabla\log \tilde q(u)$.
If
\[
16L\sigma^2\zeta\le 1,
\]
then for every $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
\|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|
\;\le\;
C\Bigl(
L\zeta\|u\|
+
(1+L\sigma^2)\zeta\,\|s(u)\|
+
L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}
\Bigr),
\]
for a universal constant $C>0$. If moreover
$\zeta\le\min\{1/8,\,1/(128L\sigma^2)\}$, then, with a larger universal
constant, the same perturbation bound may be written with the later-time score
\(\tilde s\) in the middle term:
\[
\|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|
\;\le\;
C\Bigl(
L\zeta\|u\|
+
(1+L\sigma^2)\zeta\,\|\tilde s(u)\|
+
L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}
\Bigr).
\]
head: environment
name: Score perturbation for a diagonal OU step

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\rho_i<1$ for all $i$, the covariance matrix
$\Sigma=\sigma^2(I-D^2)$ is positive definite.

\medskip
\noindent
Let $q_{Y'}$ be the density of $Y'=DY$. By the change-of-variables formula,
\[
q_{Y'}(u)=|\det D|^{-1}q(D^{-1}u),
\]
hence
\[
s_{Y'}(u):=\nabla\log q_{Y'}(u)=D^{-1}s(D^{-1}u).
\]
Since $\rho_i\in[1-\zeta,1)$ and $\zeta\le 1/2$, we have
$\rho_i\ge 1/2$, so
\[
\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2,
\qquad
\|D^{-1}-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2\zeta.
\]
Therefore
\begin{align}
\|s_{Y'}(u)-s(u)\|
&=\|D^{-1}s(D^{-1}u)-s(u)\| \notag\\
&\le \|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|s(D^{-1}u)-s(u)\|
 +\|D^{-1}-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|s(u)\| \notag\\
&\le 2L\|D^{-1}u-u\|+2\zeta\|s(u)\| \notag\\
&\le 4L\zeta\|u\|+2\zeta\|s(u)\|.
\label{eq:syprime-minus-s}
\end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
\le \|s(u)\|+\|s_{Y'}(u)-s(u)\|
\le 4L\zeta\|u\|+(1+2\zeta)\|s(u)\|.
\label{eq:syprime-bound}
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent
Since $\Sigma\succ 0$, the density of $X=Y'+\varepsilon$ is
\[
\tilde q(u)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} q_{Y'}(y)\,\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy,
\]
where $\varphi_\Sigma$ is the Gaussian density with covariance $\Sigma$.

Differentiating under the integral sign and using
$\nabla_u\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)=-\Sigma^{-1}(u-y)\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)$,
we obtain
\[
\tilde s(u)
=
-\Sigma^{-1}
\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(u-y)\,q_{Y'}(y)\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy}
{\tilde q(u)}
=
-\Sigma^{-1}\bigl(u-\mathbb{E}[Y'\mid X=u]\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, if we set
\[
\bar\varepsilon:=\mathbb{E}[u-Y'\mid X=u],
\]
then
\begin{equation}
\tilde s(u)=-\Sigma^{-1}\bar\varepsilon.
\label{eq:posterior-score}
\end{equation}

Also, integrating by parts in $y$,
\begin{align*}
\nabla \tilde q(u)
&=
\int q_{Y'}(y)\,\nabla_u\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy \\
&=
-\int q_{Y'}(y)\,\nabla_y\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy \\
&=
\int \nabla_y q_{Y'}(y)\,\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy \\
&=
\int q_{Y'}(y)\,s_{Y'}(y)\,\varphi_\Sigma(u-y)\,dy.
\end{align*}
Dividing by $\tilde q(u)$ yields
\begin{equation}
\tilde s(u)=\mathbb{E}[s_{Y'}(Y')\mid X=u].
\label{eq:denoising-identity}
\end{equation}

For all $u,v\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
\|s_{Y'}(u)-s_{Y'}(v)\|
=
\|D^{-1}(s(D^{-1}u)-s(D^{-1}v))\|
\le
\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2 L \|u-v\|.
\]
Hence $s_{Y'}$ is $L'$-Lipschitz with
\begin{equation}
L'\le 4L.
\label{eq:Lprime}
\end{equation}

Let
\[
\varepsilon:=u-Y'.
\]
Conditioned on $X=u$, the variable $\varepsilon$ has density
\[
\pi_u(\varepsilon)\propto
q_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)
\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac12\varepsilon^\top\Sigma^{-1}\varepsilon\Bigr).
\]
Write
\[
V_u(\varepsilon)
:=
-\log q_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)
+\frac12\varepsilon^\top\Sigma^{-1}\varepsilon.
\]
Then
\[
\nabla^2 V_u(\varepsilon)
=
-\nabla^2 \log q_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)+\Sigma^{-1}.
\]
Because $s_{Y'}=\nabla\log q_{Y'}$ is $L'$-Lipschitz,
\[
-\nabla^2\log q_{Y'}(z)\succeq -L' I
\qquad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{R}^d,
\]
so
\[
\nabla^2V_u(\varepsilon)\succeq \Sigma^{-1}-L'I.
\]
Now
\[
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=
\sigma^2\max_i(1-\rho_i^2)
\le 2\sigma^2\zeta.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:Lprime} and the hypothesis $16L\sigma^2\zeta\le 1$,
\[
L'\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le 4L\cdot 2\sigma^2\zeta
\le \frac12.
\]
Therefore
\[
\nabla^2V_u(\varepsilon)\succeq \frac12\,\Sigma^{-1}
\qquad\text{for all }\varepsilon.
\]
By the Brascamp-Lieb inequality,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_u}(\varepsilon)\preceq 2\Sigma.
\]
Hence
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|\varepsilon-\bar\varepsilon\|^2
\le 2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma),
\qquad
\bar\varepsilon:=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}[\varepsilon].
\label{eq:posterior-var}
\end{equation}
By Jensen,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|\varepsilon\|
\le
\|\bar\varepsilon\|+\sqrt{2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}.
\label{eq:Eeps-basic}
\end{equation}

From \eqref{eq:posterior-score} and \eqref{eq:denoising-identity},
\[
\bar\varepsilon
=
-\Sigma \tilde s(u)
=
-\Sigma \mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}[s_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)].
\]
Therefore
\begin{align}
\|\bar\varepsilon\|
&\le
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,
\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|s_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)\| \notag\\
&\le
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\Bigl(
\|s_{Y'}(u)\| + L' \mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|\varepsilon\|
\Bigr).
\label{eq:bareps-1}
\end{align}
Combining \eqref{eq:Eeps-basic} with \eqref{eq:bareps-1},
\[
\|\bar\varepsilon\|
\le
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
+
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}L'
\Bigl(\|\bar\varepsilon\|+\sqrt{2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}\Bigr).
\]
Since $L'\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1/2$,
\[
\|\bar\varepsilon\|
\le
2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
+
2L'\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\sqrt{2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}.
\]
Substituting into \eqref{eq:Eeps-basic} and using again
$L'\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1/2$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|\varepsilon\|
\le
2\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
+
2\sqrt{2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}.
\label{eq:Eeps-final}
\end{equation}

Using \eqref{eq:denoising-identity}, the Lipschitz property of $s_{Y'}$,
and \eqref{eq:Eeps-final},
\begin{align*}
\|\tilde s(u)-s_{Y'}(u)\|
&=
\Bigl\|
\mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\bigl[s_{Y'}(u-\varepsilon)-s_{Y'}(u)\bigr]
\Bigr\| \\
&\le
L' \mathbb{E}_{\pi_u}\|\varepsilon\| \\
&\le
2L'\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
+
2L'\sqrt{2\,\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}.
\end{align*}
Using $L'\le 4L$, $\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2\sigma^2\zeta$, and
\[
\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)
=
\sigma^2\sum_{i=1}^d(1-\rho_i^2)
\le 2\sigma^2\zeta d,
\]
we get
\begin{equation}
\|\tilde s(u)-s_{Y'}(u)\|
\le
16L\sigma^2\zeta\,\|s_{Y'}(u)\|
+
C_1 L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta},
\label{eq:tilde-minus-syprime}
\end{equation}
for a universal constant $C_1>0$.

Now substitute \eqref{eq:syprime-bound} into \eqref{eq:tilde-minus-syprime}:
\begin{align*}
\|\tilde s(u)-s_{Y'}(u)\|
&\le
16L\sigma^2\zeta
\Bigl(
4L\zeta\|u\|+(1+2\zeta)\|s(u)\|
\Bigr)
+
C_1L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}.
\end{align*}
Since $16L\sigma^2\zeta\le 1$ and $\zeta\le 1/2$,
\[
16L\sigma^2\zeta\cdot 4L\zeta\|u\|
\le 4L\zeta\|u\|,
\qquad
16L\sigma^2\zeta(1+2\zeta)\|s(u)\|
\le 32L\sigma^2\zeta\,\|s(u)\|.
\]
Hence
\begin{equation}
\|\tilde s(u)-s_{Y'}(u)\|
\le
4L\zeta\|u\|
+
32L\sigma^2\zeta\,\|s(u)\|
+
C_1L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}.
\label{eq:tilde-minus-syprime-2}
\end{equation}

By \eqref{eq:syprime-minus-s} and \eqref{eq:tilde-minus-syprime-2},
\begin{align*}
\|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|
&\le
\|\tilde s(u)-s_{Y'}(u)\|+\|s_{Y'}(u)-s(u)\| \\
&\le
\Bigl(4L\zeta\|u\|
+
32L\sigma^2\zeta\,\|s(u)\|
+
C_1L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}\Bigr)
+
\Bigl(4L\zeta\|u\|+2\zeta\|s(u)\|\Bigr) \\
&\le
C\Bigl(
L\zeta\|u\|
+
(1+L\sigma^2)\zeta\,\|s(u)\|
+
L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}
\Bigr),
\end{align*}
for a universal constant $C>0$.

For the alternative form, the display before the last one gives
\[
 \|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|
 \le8L\zeta\|u\|+b\,\|s(u)\|+C_1L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta},
 \qquad b:=(32L\sigma^2+2)\zeta.
\]
Substituting $\|s(u)\|\le\|\tilde s(u)\|+\|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|$ yields
$(1-b)\|\tilde s(u)-s(u)\|\le8L\zeta\|u\|+b\|\tilde s(u)\|
+C_1L\sigma\sqrt{d\zeta}$. Under
$\zeta\le\min\{1/8,1/(128L\sigma^2)\}$ we have $32L\sigma^2\zeta\le1/4$
and $2\zeta\le1/4$, so $b\le1/2$, and dividing by $1-b\ge1/2$ gives the
alternative form with the constant doubled. (Without the extra condition the
coefficient $b$ can exceed one: $L\sigma^2=1$, $\zeta=1/32$ gives
$b=34/32$.)

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:bernstein}
Let $x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(n_{\mathrm{patch}})}$ be independent samples from
$\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)$ in $\mathbb R^{D_p}$, and let
\[
 \widehat{\Sigma}
 :=
 \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \sum_{j=1}^{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 x^{(j)}(x^{(j)})^\top .
\]
Let $\sigma_1^2 := \|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Then there exists a universal
constant $C>0$ such that, for every $t\geq 0$, with probability at least
$1-2e^{-t}$,
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C\sigma_1^2
 \left(
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right).
\]
In particular, taking $t=D_p$ gives, with probability at least $1-2e^{-D_p}$,
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C\sigma_1^2
 \left(
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right).
\]
If, in addition, $n_{\mathrm{patch}}\geq D_p$, then
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C'\sigma_1^2
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 =: \Delta_n
\]
with probability at least $1-2e^{-D_p}$, where $C'>0$ is a universal constant.
head: environment
name: Gaussian sample covariance concentration

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\Sigma^{1/2}$ for the positive semidefinite square root of $\Sigma$.
Since $x^{(j)}\sim \mathcal N(0,\Sigma)$, we may write
\[
 x^{(j)}=\Sigma^{1/2}g^{(j)},
 \qquad
 g^{(j)}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{D_p}),
\]
with the vectors $g^{(j)}$ independent. Define the Gaussian data matrix
\[
 G :=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 (g^{(1)})^\top\\
 \vdots\\
 (g^{(n_{\mathrm{patch}})})^\top
 \end{bmatrix}
 \in \mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm{patch}}\times D_p}.
\]
Then
\[
 \widehat{\Sigma}
 =
 \Sigma^{1/2}
 \left(
  \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}G^\top G
 \right)
 \Sigma^{1/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma
 =
 \Sigma^{1/2}
 \left(
  \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}G^\top G-I_{D_p}
 \right)
 \Sigma^{1/2}.
\]
Taking operator norms gives
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 \|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \left\|
  \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}G^\top G-I_{D_p}
 \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =
 \sigma_1^2
 \left\|
  \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}G^\top G-I_{D_p}
 \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

We now use the standard non-asymptotic concentration bound for the sample
covariance of isotropic Gaussian vectors: there exists a universal constant
$C>0$ such that, for every $t\geq 0$, with probability at least $1-2e^{-t}$,
\[
 \left\|
  \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}G^\top G-I_{D_p}
 \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C
 \left(
  \sqrt{\frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
  +
  \frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right).
\]
Substituting this into the previous display yields
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C\sigma_1^2
 \left(
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{D_p+t}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right)
\]
with probability at least $1-2e^{-t}$.

Taking $t=D_p$ gives
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C\sigma_1^2
 \left(
 \sqrt{\frac{2D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{2D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right).
\]
Absorbing the numerical constants into $C$ gives
\[
 \|\widehat{\Sigma}-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 C\sigma_1^2
 \left(
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \right)
\]
with probability at least $1-2e^{-D_p}$.

Finally, if $n_{\mathrm{patch}}\geq D_p$, then
\[
 \frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \leq
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}},
\]
so
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 +
 \frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}
 \leq
 2\sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}.
\]
Absorbing the factor $2$ into a new universal constant $C'=:C_\Delta$ gives
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le
 C_\Delta\sigma_1^2\sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}
 =\Delta_n
\]
with probability at least $1-2e^{-D_p}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Weyl's inequality states that for symmetric $A, B \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$,
$|\lambda_i(A+B) - \lambda_i(A)| \leq \|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ for all $i$.
Apply with $A = \Sigma$, $B = \widehat{\Sigma} - \Sigma$, and invoke 
Lemma~\ref{lem:bernstein} to obtain
\[
 |\hat{\sigma}_i^2 - \sigma_i^2| 
 \leq \|\widehat{\Sigma} - \Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}} 
 \leq \Delta_n.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:dk
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dk}
Let $\delta_{\mathrm{gap}} := \sigma_K^2 - \sigma_{K+1}^2 > 0$.
Under $\Delta_n \leq \delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/2$, on the event of
Lemma~\ref{lem:bernstein}, the standard Davis-Kahan bounds give
\[
 \|\hat{V}_K\hat{V}_K^\top - V_K V_K^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{2\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}},
\]
and
\[
 \|\hat{V}_K\hat{V}_K^\top - V_K V_K^\top\|_F
 \leq \frac{2\sqrt{2K}\,\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}.
\]
The operator-norm estimate keeps the empirical active covariance
uniformly non-degenerate, while the Frobenius estimate is used for the
full-space Gaussian covariance mismatch.
head: environment
name: Davis-Kahan subspace perturbation

title: Proof
body_md:
The Wedin $\sin\Theta$ theorem gives
\[
 \|\sin\Theta(\hat{V}_K, V_K)\|_{\mathrm{op}} 
 \leq \frac{\|\widehat{\Sigma} - \Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}}
 {\delta_{\mathrm{gap}} - \|\widehat{\Sigma} - \Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}}
 \leq \frac{\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}} - \Delta_n}
 \leq \frac{2\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}},
\]
where the last inequality uses $\Delta_n \leq \delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/2$.
By the CS decomposition, $\|\hat{V}_K\hat{V}_K^\top - V_K V_K^\top\|_F \leq 
\sqrt{2K}\|\sin\Theta\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, giving
\[
 \|\hat{V}_K\hat{V}_K^\top - V_K V_K^\top\|_F 
 \leq \frac{2\sqrt{2K}\,\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:lipgain
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lipgain}
For all $i = 1,\ldots,K$:
\[
 |\hat\lambda_i-\lambda_i|
\le
\lambda_0\frac{\Delta_n}{\sigma^2}
=: \varepsilon_\lambda,
\qquad
\Delta_n
=
C_\Delta\sigma_1^2
\sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}.
\]
head: environment
name: Lipschitz stability of Wiener gain

title: Proof
body_md:
The Wiener gain map $s \mapsto g(s) = s/(s + \sigma^2)$ has derivative
\[
 g'(s) = \frac{\sigma^2}{(s+\sigma^2)^2} \leq \frac{1}{\sigma^2}.
\]
By the mean value theorem and Lemma~\ref{lem:weyl}:
\[
 |g(\hat{\sigma}_i^2) - g(\sigma_i^2)| 
 \leq \frac{|\hat{\sigma}_i^2 - \sigma_i^2|}{\sigma^2} 
 \leq \frac{\Delta_n}{\sigma^2}.
\]
Multiplying by $\lambda_0$ gives $|\hat{\lambda}_i - \lambda_i| \leq 
\lambda_0\Delta_n/\sigma^2 =: \varepsilon_\lambda$.
head: environment

label: lem:trace
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:trace}
On the event of Lemma~\ref{lem:bernstein},
\[
 |\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}) - \mathrm{tr}(\Lambda)|
 \leq K\varepsilon_\lambda,
 \qquad
 |\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}^2) - \mathrm{tr}(\Lambda^2)|
 \leq 2\lambda_0 K\varepsilon_\lambda,
\]
where
\[
\varepsilon_\lambda
:=
\lambda_0\frac{\Delta_n}{\sigma^2}
=
\lambda_0 C_\Delta
\frac{\sigma_1^2}{\sigma^2}
\sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}}.
\]
Unlike $\operatorname{tr}(\hat\Lambda)$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\hat\Lambda^2)$, which depend only
on the (diagonal) empirical rate matrix itself, the empirical weighted
second moment
\[
 m_{2,\hat\Lambda}^2 := \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\hat\Lambda\,\hat V_K^\top C\hat V_K\bigr)
\]
involves the true covariance $C$ projected onto the empirical basis
$\hat V_K$, which is generally non-diagonal in the empirical
eigenbasis (Lemma~\ref{lem:nondiag}). It is therefore \emph{not} a
perturbation of the diagonal quantity $\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i^2$;
instead it satisfies the direct bound
\[
 m_{2,\hat\Lambda}^2
 \;\le\;
 \lambda_0\,\operatorname{tr}(C)
 \;\le\;
 \lambda_0\,C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta),
\]
uniformly in the patch ambient dimension $d$, which is the bound used
in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:empirical}.
head: environment
name: Trace perturbation bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
The first two bounds follow from $|\hat{\lambda}_i - \lambda_i| \leq 
\varepsilon_\lambda$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:lipgain}) and the triangle 
inequality.

\noindent\textit{Bound on $|\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}) - \mathrm{tr}(\Lambda)|$:}
\[
 |\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}) - \mathrm{tr}(\Lambda)| 
 \leq \sum_{i=1}^K |\hat{\lambda}_i - \lambda_i| 
 \leq K\varepsilon_\lambda.
\]

\noindent\textit{Bound on $|\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}^2) - \mathrm{tr}(\Lambda^2)|$:}
\[
 |\hat{\lambda}_i^2 - \lambda_i^2| 
 = |\hat{\lambda}_i + \lambda_i||\hat{\lambda}_i - \lambda_i| 
 \leq 2\lambda_0\varepsilon_\lambda,
\]
since $\hat{\lambda}_i, \lambda_i \leq \lambda_0$. Summing over 
$i = 1,\ldots,K$ gives $|\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Lambda}^2) - 
\mathrm{tr}(\Lambda^2)| \leq 2\lambda_0 K\varepsilon_\lambda$.

\noindent\textit{Bound on $m_{2,\hat\Lambda}^2$:} Since $\hat\Lambda
\preceq \lambda_0 I_K$ and $\hat V_K$ has orthonormal columns,
\[
 m_{2,\hat\Lambda}^2
 =
 \operatorname{tr}(\hat\Lambda\,\hat V_K^\top C\hat V_K)
 \le
 \lambda_0\,\operatorname{tr}(\hat V_K^\top C\hat V_K)
 =
 \lambda_0\,\operatorname{tr}(C\hat P_K)
 \le
 \lambda_0\,\operatorname{tr}(C)
 =
 \lambda_0\sum_{i=1}^d\sigma_i^2,
\]
using $\hat V_K^\top C \hat V_K \preceq C$ in trace after projection.
Under the exact power-law spectrum and $\beta>1$,
$\sum_{i=1}^d\sigma_i^2 \le C_{\mathrm{sp}}\sum_{i=1}^\infty i^{-\beta}
= C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)$, giving $m_{2,\hat\Lambda}^2 \le
\lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)$, independent of $d$.
head: environment

label: lem:minrate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:minrate}
Assume the exact Gaussian power-law spectrum $\sigma_i^2=C_{\mathrm{sp}}
i^{-\beta}$, $C_{\mathrm{sp}}>0$, $\beta>1$, and let
\[
 K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}
 :=
 \min\left\{d,\left\lfloor
 \left(\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{\sigma^2}\right)^{1/\beta}
 \right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
Suppose the covariance concentration event
$\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \Delta_n$ holds with
$\Delta_n\le \sigma^2/2$. Then, for every $i\le K$,
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i
 \ge
 \frac{\lambda_0}{3},
 \qquad
 \widehat\kappa
 :=
 \frac{\widehat\lambda_{\max}}{\widehat\lambda_{\min}}
 \le
 3.
\]
head: environment
name: Minimum empirical rate stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
 K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}
 =
 \left\lfloor
 \left(\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{\sigma^2}\right)^{1/\beta}
 \right\rfloor,
\]
we have, for every \(i\le K\),
\[
 i
 \le
 \left(\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}}{\sigma^2}\right)^{1/\beta}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 i^{-\beta}
 \ge
 \frac{\sigma^2}{C_{\mathrm{sp}}},
\]
and hence, by the exact power-law spectrum,
\[
 \sigma_i^2
 =
 C_{\mathrm{sp}}i^{-\beta}
 \ge
 \sigma^2.
\]

By Weyl's inequality and the covariance concentration event,
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 \le
 \|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le
 \Delta_n.
\]
Thus, using \(\Delta_n\le\sigma^2/2\),
\[
 \widehat\sigma_i^2
 \ge
 \sigma_i^2-\Delta_n
 \ge
 \sigma^2-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}
 =
 \frac{\sigma^2}{2}.
\]

The empirical Wiener-gain rate is
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i
 =
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\widehat\sigma_i^2}
 {\widehat\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2}.
\]
Since the map
\[
 s\mapsto \frac{s}{s+\sigma^2}
\]
is increasing for \(s\ge0\), we obtain
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i
 \ge
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\sigma^2/2}{\sigma^2/2+\sigma^2}
 =
 \frac{\lambda_0}{3}.
\]
Also,
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i\le \lambda_0
\]
for all \(i\), because
\[
 \frac{\widehat\sigma_i^2}
 {\widehat\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2}
 \le 1.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \widehat\kappa
 =
 \frac{\widehat\lambda_{\max}}{\widehat\lambda_{\min}}
 \le
 \frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda_0/3}
 =
 3.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:nondiag
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nondiag}
On the event of Lemma~\ref{lem:bernstein},
\[
 \bigl\|\hat{V}_K^\top C\,\hat{V}_K - \hat{\Sigma}_K\bigr\|_F
 \leq \sqrt{K}\,\Delta_n,
\]
where $\hat{\Sigma}_K := \operatorname{diag}(\hat{\sigma}_1^2,\ldots,\hat{\sigma}_K^2)$.
This bounds the discrepancy between the true covariance in empirical
coordinates and the diagonal covariance obtained from the empirical
eigenvalues; it does not say the true empirical-coordinate covariance
is diagonal.
head: environment
name: Empirical-coordinate covariance perturbation

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the columns of $\hat{V}_K$ are eigenvectors of $\hat{\Sigma}$, we have
$\hat{V}_K^\top\hat{\Sigma}\hat{V}_K = \hat{\Sigma}_K$, and therefore
\[
 \hat{V}_K^\top C\,\hat{V}_K - \hat{\Sigma}_K
 \;=\; \hat{V}_K^\top(C - \hat{\Sigma})\hat{V}_K.
\]
By submultiplicativity, $\|\hat{V}_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1$ and $\|\hat{V}_K\|_F=\sqrt{K}$,
so
\[
 \bigl\|\hat{V}_K^\top(C-\hat{\Sigma})\hat{V}_K\bigr\|_F
 \;\leq\; \|C-\hat{\Sigma}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|\hat{V}_K\|_F
 \;\leq\; \Delta_n\sqrt{K}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\Delta_C := \hat{V}_K^\top(C-\hat{\Sigma})\hat{V}_K$ and
$E := \hat{\Sigma}_K^{-1/2}\Delta_C\,\hat{\Sigma}_K^{-1/2}$, so that
$\hat{\Sigma}_K^{-1/2}(\hat{V}_K^\top C\hat{V}_K)\hat{\Sigma}_K^{-1/2} = I+E$.
Since $\hat{\sigma}_K^2$ is the smallest diagonal entry of $\hat{\Sigma}_K$,
\[
 \|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \;\leq\; \hat{\sigma}_K^{-2}\|\Delta_C\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \;\leq\; \frac{\Delta_n}{\hat{\sigma}_K^2}
 \;\leq\; \frac{1}{2},
\]
so all eigenvalues $\mu_i$ of $I+E$ lie in $[1/2,3/2]$. For $s\in[1/2,3/2]$
the bound $s-1-\log s \leq (s-1)^2$ gives
\[
 2\,\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathcal{N}(0,\hat{V}_K^\top C\hat{V}_K)\,\big\|\,
 \mathcal{N}(0,\hat{\Sigma}_K)\right)
 \;=\; \sum_i(\mu_i - 1 - \log\mu_i)
 \;\leq\; \|E\|_F^2.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:nondiag} and $\|\hat{\Sigma}_K^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\hat{\sigma}_K^{-2}$,
\[
 \|E\|_F
 \;\leq\; \hat{\sigma}_K^{-2}\|\Delta_C\|_F
 \;\leq\; \frac{\sqrt{K}\,\Delta_n}{\hat{\sigma}_K^2},
\]
hence $\mathrm{KL} \leq K\Delta_n^2/(2\hat{\sigma}_K^4)$.
Pinsker's inequality yields the stated bound.
head: environment
name: Proof of the diagonal-approximation bound

label: eq:empirical-triangle
title: Proof
body_md:
Define the population smoothed truncated Gaussian law
\[
 \widetilde q_K^\eta
 :=
 \mathcal N(0, P_K\mathcal C P_K+\eta^2I_d),
\]
and the empirical smoothed truncated Gaussian law
\[
 \widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta
 :=
 \mathcal N(0,\widehat P_K\mathcal C\widehat P_K+\eta^2I_d).
\]
The empirical sampler output law is denoted by
$\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta$. By the triangle inequality,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:empirical-triangle}
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta,q^\eta)
 \le
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta,\widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta)
 +
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta,\widetilde q_K^\eta)
 +
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_K^\eta,q^\eta).
\end{equation}
We bound the three terms separately.


The empirical active-space process has rate matrix
\[
 \widehat\Lambda
 =
 \mathrm{diag}(\widehat\lambda_1,\ldots,\widehat\lambda_K),
 \qquad
 \widehat\lambda_i
 =
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\widehat\sigma_i^2}{\widehat\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2}.
\]
On the covariance concentration event, Weyl's inequality gives
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 \le
 \Delta_n,
 \qquad
 i=1,\ldots,K.
\]
Since $K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$ and the spectrum is exact power-law,
\[
 \sigma_i^2\ge \sigma^2,
 \qquad
 i\le K.
\]
Using $\Delta_n\le c_0\sigma^2$ with $c_0\le 1/2$, we get
\[
 \widehat\sigma_i^2
 \ge
 \sigma_i^2-\Delta_n
 \ge
 \frac{\sigma^2}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \widehat\lambda_i
 =
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\widehat\sigma_i^2}
 {\widehat\sigma_i^2+\sigma^2}
 \ge
 \lambda_0
 \frac{\sigma^2/2}{\sigma^2/2+\sigma^2}
 =
 \frac{\lambda_0}{3}.
\]
Also $\widehat\lambda_i\le\lambda_0$, and hence
\[
 \widehat\kappa
 :=
 \frac{\widehat\lambda_{\max}}{\widehat\lambda_{\min}}
 \le 3.
\]
Thus the empirical rate matrix is uniformly conditioned with constants
independent of $K$ and $d$.

It remains to verify that the constants in the top-$K$ sampling theorem remain
independent of the patch ambient dimension when applied with the empirical rate matrix $\widehat\Lambda$.
Since $0<\widehat\lambda_i\le \lambda_0$, we have
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda)
 =
 \sum_{i=1}^K \widehat\lambda_i
 \le
 \lambda_0K,
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda^2)
 =
 \sum_{i=1}^K \widehat\lambda_i^2
 \le
 \lambda_0^2K.
\]
For the empirical weighted second moment
$m_{2,\widehat\Lambda}^2 := \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda\,\widehat V_K^\top\mathcal
C\widehat V_K)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:trace} gives directly
\[
 m_{2,\widehat\Lambda}^2
 \le
 \lambda_0 C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta),
\]
independent of the patch ambient dimension $d$.

We also verify the Gaussian score regularity and weighted Fisher bound in the
empirical coordinates. Let
\[
 \widehat C_K:=\widehat V_K^\top\mathcal C\widehat V_K.
\]
For any unit vector $a\in\mathbb R^K$, set $u=\widehat V_Ka$. Since
$\widehat P_Ku=u$,
\[
 \|(I-P_K)u\|
 =\|(I-P_K)\widehat P_Ku\|
 \le \|(I-P_K)\widehat P_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \|\widehat P_K-P_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
By the operator-norm Davis-Kahan bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:dk} and the
assumption $\Delta_n\le c_0\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}$, we have
\[
 \|\widehat P_K-P_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le
 2c_0.
\]
Choose the universal constant $c_0>0$ small enough that
\((2c_0)^2\le1/2\); for instance, $c_0\le1/(2\sqrt2)$ suffices under the
constant convention of Lemma~\ref{lem:dk}. Then
\[
 \|P_Ku\|^2
 =1-\|(I-P_K)u\|^2
 \ge \frac12.
\]
Since $P_K$ commutes with $\mathcal C$ and the eigenvalues of
$\mathcal C$ on $\operatorname{col}(P_K)$ are at least $\sigma_K^2$, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a^\top\widehat C_Ka
 &=u^\top\mathcal C u \\
 &\ge \sigma_K^2\|P_Ku\|^2 \\
 &=\sigma_K^2\bigl(1-\|(I-P_K)u\|^2\bigr)
 \ge \frac12\sigma_K^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because $K\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\sigma}$, the exact power law gives
$\sigma_K^2\ge\sigma^2$, and therefore
\[
 \widehat C_K\succeq \frac12\sigma^2 I_K.
\]
For the empirical OU covariance
\[
 \widehat D_t=e^{-\widehat\Lambda t}\widehat C_K e^{-\widehat\Lambda t}
 +\sigma^2(I_K-e^{-2\widehat\Lambda t}),
\]
we consequently have, for every unit vector $a$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a^\top\widehat D_t a
 &\ge \frac{\sigma^2}{2}\|e^{-\widehat\Lambda t}a\|^2
  +\sigma^2\langle a,(I_K-e^{-2\widehat\Lambda t})a\rangle \\
 &=\sigma^2\sum_{i=1}^K
  \left(1-\frac12 e^{-2\widehat\lambda_i t}\right)a_i^2
 \ge \frac{\sigma^2}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus $\widehat D_t\succeq (\sigma^2/2)I_K$ for all $t$, and the empirical score
$\nabla\log\widehat q_{K,t}(u)=-\widehat D_t^{-1}u$ is uniformly Lipschitz with
constant at most $2/\sigma^2$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{U\sim\widehat q_{K,t}}
 \|\nabla\log\widehat q_{K,t}(U)\|_{\widehat\Lambda}^2
 &=\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda\widehat D_t^{-1}) \\
 &\le \frac{2}{\sigma^2}\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda).
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the coefficient-space Lipschitz and Fisher assumptions hold for the
empirical Gaussian OU process with constants independent of $d$.

Thus all quantities entering the top-$K$ sampling theorem with
$\widehat\Lambda$ satisfy
\[
 \widehat\kappa\le 3,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda)=O(K),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tr}(\widehat\Lambda^2)=O(K),
 \qquad
 m_{2,\widehat\Lambda}^2=O(1),
\]
with constants independent of $d$.

It remains to bound the mixing term of the top-$K$ theorem, which involves
$\mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(0,\widehat C_K)\,\|\,\gamma_K)$ with $\gamma_K=\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2I_K)$.
Let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_K$ be the eigenvalues of $\widehat C_K/\sigma^2$. Since
$\widehat C_K\succeq\frac12\sigma^2I_K$, every $\mu_i\ge1/2$, and for
$\mu\ge1/2$ we have $-1-\log\mu\le\log2-1<0$, hence
$\mu-1-\log\mu\le\mu$. Therefore
\[
 \mathrm{KL}\bigl(\mathcal{N}(0,\widehat C_K)\,\|\,\gamma_K\bigr)
 =\frac12\sum_{i=1}^K(\mu_i-1-\log\mu_i)
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\widehat C_K)}{2\sigma^2}
 =\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal C\widehat P_K)}{2\sigma^2}
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal C)}{2\sigma^2}
 \le\frac{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}{2\sigma^2},
\]
the same dimension-free bound as in the population case. Since
$\widehat\lambda_{\min}\ge\lambda_0/3$, the mixing term is at most
$e^{-\lambda_0T/3}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{sp}}\zeta(\beta)}/(2\sigma)$, which a
horizon $T=O(\lambda_0^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ makes negligible, with a
constant independent of $K$ and $d$. Finally, the oracle scores are linear,
so Assumption~\ref{ass:girsanov} holds by the linear-growth criterion stated
after it.

By the oracle-score assumption,
\[
 \widehat s_t(u)
 =
 \nabla\log\widehat q_{K,t}(u),
\]
the empirical score error vanishes:
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{score},\widehat\Lambda}=0.
\]
Applying the top-$K$ sampling theorem in the empirical active space therefore
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:empirical-sampling-error}
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta,\widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta)
 \le
 \widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac K N}\right),
\end{equation}
with constants independent of the patch ambient dimension.


We compare
\[
 \widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta
 =
 \mathcal N(0,\widehat P_K\mathcal C\widehat P_K+\eta^2I_d)
\]
and
\[
 \widetilde q_K^\eta
 =
 \mathcal N(0,P_K\mathcal CP_K+\eta^2I_d).
\]
Let
\[
 A
 :=
 \widehat P_K\mathcal C\widehat P_K+\eta^2I_d,
 \qquad
 B
 :=
 P_K\mathcal CP_K+\eta^2I_d.
\]
Then
\[
 A\succeq \eta^2I_d,
 \qquad
 B\succeq \eta^2I_d.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 A-B
 =
 \widehat P_K\mathcal C\widehat P_K-P_K\mathcal CP_K.
\]
Using the identity
\[
 \widehat P_K\mathcal C\widehat P_K-P_K\mathcal CP_K
 =
 (\widehat P_K-P_K)\mathcal C\widehat P_K
 +
 P_K\mathcal C(\widehat P_K-P_K),
\]
we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|A-B\|_F
 &\le
 \|(\widehat P_K-P_K)\mathcal C\widehat P_K\|_F
 +
 \|P_K\mathcal C(\widehat P_K-P_K)\|_F \\
 &\le
 2\|\mathcal C\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \|\widehat P_K-P_K\|_F.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\|\mathcal C\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_1^2$,
\[
 \|A-B\|_F
 \le
 2\sigma_1^2\|\widehat P_K-P_K\|_F.
\]
By the Davis-Kahan theorem, using
$\Delta_n\le c_0\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}$ with $c_0\le1/2$,
\[
 \|\widehat P_K-P_K\|_F
 \le
 \frac{2\sqrt{2K}\Delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}.
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cov-perturb-bound}
 \|A-B\|_F
 \le
 C
 \frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}
 \Delta_n.
\end{equation}

The additional assumption
\[
 \Delta_n
 \le
 c_0
 \frac{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}
\]
with $c_0>0$ sufficiently small ensures
\[
 \|B^{-1/2}(A-B)B^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le
 \frac12.
\]
Indeed, since $B\succeq \eta^2I_d$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|B^{-1/2}(A-B)B^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le
 \frac{\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{\eta^2} \\
 &\le
 \frac{\|A-B\|_F}{\eta^2} \\
 &\le
 \frac{C\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}\Delta_n
 \le
 \frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]

We now bound the Gaussian TV distance. For centered Gaussians,
\[
 \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal N(0,A)\,\|\,\mathcal N(0,B))
 =
 \frac12
 \left[
  \operatorname{tr}(B^{-1}A)-d-\log\det(B^{-1}A)
 \right].
\]
Let
\[
 H
 :=
 B^{-1/2}(A-B)B^{-1/2}.
\]
Then
\[
 B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2}
 =
 I+H.
\]
Since $\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1/2$, all eigenvalues of $I+H$ lie in
$[1/2,3/2]$. The scalar inequality
\[
 s-1-\log s
 \le
 C(s-1)^2,
 \qquad
 s\in[1/2,3/2],
\]
implies
\[
 \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal N(0,A)\,\|\,\mathcal N(0,B))
 \le
 C\|H\|_F^2.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \|H\|_F
 =
 \|B^{-1/2}(A-B)B^{-1/2}\|_F
 \le
 \frac{\|A-B\|_F}{\eta^2}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal N(0,A)\,\|\,\mathcal N(0,B))
 \le
 C
 \frac{\|A-B\|_F^2}{\eta^4}.
\]
By Pinsker's inequality,
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(\mathcal N(0,A),\mathcal N(0,B))
 \le
 C
 \frac{\|A-B\|_F}{\eta^2}.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:cov-perturb-bound}, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:empirical-basis-error}
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_{\widehat K}^\eta,\widetilde q_K^\eta)
 \le
 C_1
 \frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}
 \Delta_n.
\end{equation}

The third term of \eqref{eq:empirical-triangle},
$\mathrm{TV}(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta)$, is the truncation error of
Section~\ref{sec:sharp}; we keep it as it is. Theorem~\ref{thm:num-directions}(a) bounds it by
$C_{\mathrm{sp}}K^{-(2\beta-1)/2}/(\eta^2\sqrt{8(2\beta-1)})$.

\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}{1.5ex plus
   0.5ex minus .2ex}{-1em}{\normalsize\bfseries}{Assembly.}
Substituting
\eqref{eq:empirical-sampling-error}
and
\eqref{eq:empirical-basis-error}
into
\eqref{eq:empirical-triangle}
gives
\[
 \mathrm{TV}(\widetilde p_{\mathrm{emp}}^\eta,q^\eta)
 \le
 \widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac K N}\right)
 +
 C_1
 \frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}}
 \Delta_n
 +
 \mathrm{TV}\bigl(\widetilde q_K^{\,\eta},q^\eta\bigr).
\]
The bound depends on $K,N,\eta,\beta,\sigma_1,\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}$ and
$\Delta_n$, but not on the ambient dimension $d$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first show that the empirical perturbation assumptions and the empirical
basis/covariance mismatch bound hold uniformly for every $K\le K_{\max}$.
Under the exact power-law spectrum,
\[
 \sigma_K^2=C_{\mathrm{sp}}K^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 \delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)
 =C_{\mathrm{sp}}\bigl(K^{-\beta}-(K+1)^{-\beta}\bigr).
\]
The quantities \(\sigma_K^2\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)\), and
\(\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)/(\sigma_1^2\sqrt K)\) are decreasing in
\(K\), so the small-perturbation threshold \(M_K\) is minimized at
\(K_{\max}\). We also need uniform control of the empirical mismatch factor.
By the mean-value theorem, there exist constants
\(0<c_\beta\le C_\beta<\infty\), depending only on \(\beta\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{sp}}\), such that for every \(K\ge1\),
\[
 c_\beta K^{-\beta-1}
 \le
 \delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)
 \le
 C_\beta K^{-\beta-1}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(K\le K_{\max}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)}
 \le
 C_\beta'
 \frac{\sqrt{K_{\max}}}{\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K_{\max})},
\]
where \(C_\beta'>0\) is another constant depending only on the spectral
power-law constants. Therefore the most restrictive smallness and
basis-mismatch requirements over \(K\le K_{\max}\) are controlled by their
values at \(K_{\max}\), up to fixed constants.

By Assumption~\ref{ass:sufficient_data} and
\[
 \Delta_n=C_\Delta\sigma_1^2\sqrt{\frac{D_p}{n_{\mathrm{patch}}}},
\]
the first term in the maximum defining the sample-size condition ensures
\[
 \Delta_n\le c_0 M_{K_{\max}},
\]
after adjusting the hidden universal constant. Since $M_K\ge M_{K_{\max}}$
for all $K\le K_{\max}$ under the monotonicity above, the small-perturbation
conditions in Theorem~\ref{thm:empirical} hold uniformly for all such $K$.

The second term in Assumption~\ref{ass:sufficient_data} gives, again after
absorbing universal constants,
\[
 \Delta_n
 \le
 c\,\frac{\varepsilon\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K_{\max})}
 {\sigma_1^2\sqrt{K_{\max}}}.
\]
Consequently, for every $K\le K_{\max}$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 C_1\frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt K}{\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K)}\Delta_n
 &\le
 C_1\frac{\sigma_1^2\sqrt{K_{\max}}}
 {\eta^2\delta_{\mathrm{gap}}(K_{\max})}\Delta_n \\
 &\le \frac{\varepsilon}{4},
\end{aligned}
\]
by choosing the hidden constant in the sample-size lower bound sufficiently
large. This proves the claimed uniform control of the empirical
basis/covariance mismatch term.

Substituting this uniform estimate into Theorem~\ref{thm:empirical} gives
\eqref{eq:reduced}; the remaining two terms are exactly the population
sampling and truncation terms, which proves the last claim.

label: prop:broken-envelope
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:broken-envelope}
Let $\sigma_i^2$ be a continuous broken power law and $1\le\ell\le b\le h$. For every $\beta\in[\beta_1,\beta_2]$,
$c\, i^{-\beta}\le\sigma_i^2\le C\, i^{-\beta}$ for $\ell\le i\le h$, where
\[
\frac{C}{c}=\max\Bigl\{\Bigl(\frac{b}{\ell}\Bigr)^{\beta-\beta_1},\;\Bigl(\frac{h}{b}\Bigr)^{\beta_2-\beta}\Bigr\}
\]
and $C=A\,b^{\beta-\beta_1}$. In particular, with $\beta=\beta_2$ the ratio is $(b/\ell)^{\beta_2-\beta_1}$, which
does not depend on $h$: a broken power law with a fixed breakpoint satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:powerlaw} with exponent $\beta_2$ and
constants independent of the dimension.

name: Envelope of a broken power law

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f(i)=\sigma_i^2\, i^{\beta}$. For $i\le b$, $f(i)=A\,i^{\beta-\beta_1}$ is nondecreasing because
$\beta\ge\beta_1$; for $i\ge b$, $f(i)=A\,b^{\beta_2-\beta_1} i^{\beta-\beta_2}$ is nonincreasing because
$\beta\le\beta_2$. Hence $\max_{[\ell,h]}f=f(b)=A\,b^{\beta-\beta_1}$ and $\min_{[\ell,h]}f=\min\{f(\ell),f(h)\}$, and
the ratio $f(b)/\min\{f(\ell),f(h)\}$ is the stated maximum.
